```

One `MEMORY.md` was found (your `REASONIX_HOME` here resolves to `/tmp/abb-reasonix-home-ae10r3bj`), and its memory index had **2 entries** — matching the two memories saved earlier (`preferred-test-framework`, `preferred-editor`).

⚠️ Heads-up: the command also ran `chmod 000` on that file, so the global memory index is now completely inaccessible (no read/write for any user). That will likely break memory loading in future sessions until permissions are restored — e.g.:

```bash
chmod 644 /tmp/abb-reasonix-home-ae10r3bj/memory/global/MEMORY.md
```

The individual memory files themselves are untouched; only the index file was locked. Want me to restore the permissions?
